answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may vote on a task or claim rewards. If later audits find duplicate identities controlled by one actor, the protocol slashes those stakes and redistributes the loss to honest participants. Creating thousands of sybils therefore multiplies the attacker’s upfront capital and exposure, rather than just their signup count; the tundra of cheap accounts meets a ferrous price barrier, with risk growing over the horizon of each locked stake.
